claims.text: A risk I published in T_k03b_trajectory (CHECKPOINT-19) — 'a normal oracle run still cannot see a transient' — is now MEASURED against the shipped instrument rather than asserted. The canary was patched INTO the sim (SimWorld.step wrapper, boss_stability +40 at tick 3500, restored at 3560) and the UNMODIFIED behavioural_oracle.py was run on it: RESULT PASS, exit 0, all six assertions green including boss_stability itself at 'expected 0 (+/-0), got 0'. The shipped oracle genuinely cannot see a protected-field transient.

STRONGER THAN THE DESIGNED TEST: the K-03B audit was run in CANONICAL mode against the same infected sim — it was NOT told a canary existed and had no canary logic of its own active. It still caught the transient at tick_idx=3500 (boss_stability 300 -> 340) and exited 1. The audit therefore DETECTS an unknown transient; it does not merely confirm one it planted itself, which is the difference between a check and a rehearsal.

The two instruments disagree on identical input, which is the whole finding: same sim, same seed, same 11,901 ticks. Shipped oracle exit 0 PASS. Trajectory audit exit 1 with a named tick and a named field. End-state verification and trajectory verification are not stronger and weaker versions of each other — they are blind to different things, and the fleet was relying only on the one that is blind here.

tests.command: python3 behavioural_oracle.py  # SHIPPED, on canary-infected sim

decisions_requested: Head 06 R3 disposition, now with the measurement it asked for: the shipped oracle returns a clean PASS on a sim containing a mutated-and-restored protected authority field. If CONTINUOUS TRAJECTORY CLAIMS are to close, the audit must run somewhere a normal verification run reaches. It currently does not.
risks: The canary is injected by patching the sandbox sim, not by any product code path. It demonstrates that the oracle cannot SEE such a transient; it does not demonstrate that the product can PRODUCE one. Whether a real skill or effect could cause it is exactly K-01B, which ARM-08 owns and has not landed.

I audited 48 published risk statements to find this one. The other 47 remain a mix of measured facts, judgments, and untested assertions, and I have not classified them individually. Two of the ones I did test turned out false.
